correctness.rationale: Every positive integer with \(\Omega\le2\) is prime, a prime square, or a product of two distinct primes. The first two cases cannot be quasi-amicable members. In the last case, a hypothetical pair \(m=pq,n=rs\) gives \(n=p+q\) and \(m=r+s\), while distinct-prime products satisfy \(pq>p+q\) and \(rs>r+s\), a contradiction.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The four-distinct-prime lower bound does not dominate the new theorem, because two coprime squarefree semiprimes have exactly four distinct prime factors. Prime-power restrictions cover the square branch but not the squarefree-semiprime branch. Density zero is logically orthogonal.

Pollack's full paper proves density zero without a semiprime classification. Searches over aliases and exact tables found no equivalent or stronger statement.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete structural boundary rather than a bounded census: it eliminates the entire layer where both members have multiplicative complexity at most two. The foundational literature itself asks structural questions about prime powers and the number of prime factors, so the result closes the next missing low-complexity case and gives a useful exact search restriction.
